questions.problem: What is the amplitude of the function $f(x)=\frac{3-9\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{5}?$

First, notice that we can rewrite the function as follows:

$$
f(x)=\frac{3-9\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{5}=-\frac{9}{5}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{3}{5}

Now, given a function in the form $f(x)=A\operatorname{sin}⁡(Bx+C)+D,$ the amplitude is $|A|.$

In our case, we have that $A=-\frac{9}{5}.$ Therefore, the amplitude is $|A|=|-\frac{9}{5}|=\frac{9}{5}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Midline of a Transformed Sinusoidal Function
questions.problem: Find the equation of the midline for a transformed sine function with a minimum value of $2$ and a maximum value of $10.$
questions.worked_solution:
A sinusoidal graph's midline (or vertical shift) is the horizontal line that divides it vertically in half. 

The equation of the midline is given by

$$
y=\frac{{y}_{\text{min}}+{y}_{\text{max}}}{2},
$$

where ${y}_{\text{min}}$ and ${y}_{\text{max}}$ are the minimum and maximum values of the function. The midline equals the average of the maximum and minimum values. 

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}_{\text{min}}+{y}_{\text{max}}}{2} & =\frac{2+10}{2} \\  & =\frac{12}{2} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the midline is $y=6.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Range of a Transformed Sinusoidal Function
questions.problem: What is the range of the function $y=-4\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-{30}^{∘})+1?$
questions.worked_solution:
The range of $\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ is

$$
-1\le \operatorname{cos}⁡x\le 1.
$$

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore,

$$
-1\le \operatorname{cos}⁡(x-{30}^{∘})\le 1.
$$

Multiplying the above inequality by $-4$ and then adding $1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & -1\le \operatorname{cos}⁡(x-{30}^{∘})\le 1 \\  & 4\ge -4\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-{30}^{∘})\ge -4 \\  & 5\ge -4\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-{30}^{∘})+1\ge -3 \\  & -3\le y\le 5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the range is $y\in [-3,5].$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Range of a Transformed Sinusoidal Function
questions.problem: What is the range of the function $y=-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+{30}^{∘})+4?$
questions.worked_solution:
The range of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ is

$$
-1\le \operatorname{sin}⁡x\le 1.
$$

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore,

$$
-1\le \operatorname{sin}⁡(x+{30}^{∘})\le 1.
$$

Multiplying the above inequality by $-2$ and then adding $4$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-1 & \le \operatorname{sin}⁡(x+{30}^{∘})\le 1 \\ 2 & \ge -2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+{30}^{∘})\ge -2 \\ 6 & \ge -2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+{30}^{∘})+4\ge 2 \\ 2 & \le y\le 6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the range is $y\in [2,6].$

questions.problem: What is the range of $f(x)=3\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{6})+2?$
questions.worked_solution:
The range of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ is

$$

$$

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore,

$$
-1\le \operatorname{sin}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{6})\le 1.
$$

Multiplying the above inequality by $3$ and then adding $2$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & -1\le \operatorname{sin}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{6})\le 1 \\  & -3\le 3\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{6})\le 3 \\  & -1\le 3\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{6})+2\le 5 \\  & -1\le f(x)\le 5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the range is $f(x)\in [-1,5].$

questions.problem: Find the range of the function $y=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)-2.$
questions.worked_solution:
The range of $\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ is

$$
-1\le \operatorname{cos}⁡x\le 1.
$$

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore,

$$
-1\le \operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)\le 1.
$$

Multiplying the above inequality by $2$ and then subtracting $2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & -1\le \operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)\le 1 \\  & -2\le 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)\le 2 \\  & -4\le 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)-2\le 0 \\  & -4\le y\le 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the range is $y\in [-4,0].$

$$

canonical_examples.problem: What is the range of the function $f(x) = -4\cos(3x)-2?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The range of $\cos x$ is

$$
-1 \leq \cos x \leq 1.
$$

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore,

$$
-1\leq\cos\left(3x \right) \leq 1.
$$

Multiplying the above inequality by $-4$ and then subtracting $2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-1 & \le \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\le 1 \\ 4 & \ge -4\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\ge -4 \\ 2 & \ge -4\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)-2\ge -6 \\ -6 & \le f(x)\le 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the range is $f(x)\in [-6,2].$
